$about: The Labs page (examples/labs.html, my-3d2dge.vercel.app/labs) is built from this list by tools/build.mjs. Each entry is one page: page is an examples/ page name (examples/<page>.html, served at /<page>) or a dist/ path; links are [label, what to add to the address]. keep: tools and demos worth keeping. temporary: one-off comparisons and experiments, each with the date it was added and the question it answers; when the question is settled, delete the page and its entry. tools/labs-test.mjs opens every link.

entries.title: Emberdeep
entries.what: The game itself. Its own test areas are inside it: the Proving Grounds, the Gallery (every monster, skill and pose) and the Developer panel's sandbox.

entries.title: Mocap Lab
entries.what: Every imported animation clip, on a mannequin and on the hero, in every view, slow or frame by frame. Sets: Quaternius, Mesh2Motion, CMU motion capture, and the clips the hero uses; the CMU library holds every one of its 2,548 takes.

entries.title: Perspective Lab
entries.what: One room in every camera view (isometric, three-quarter, top-down, brawler, side), with skeleton and lighting toggles.

entries.title: Stress test
entries.what: Raise the load (up to 5,000 monsters, torches, particles) until the frame rate drops, or run the benchmark to rate this device. Any view the engine can draw (side scrolling, with depth drawn the Mode 7 way, or a custom turn and tilt), fixed in place if you like, and the same camera opens on the 3D stress test.

entries.title: Emberwell
entries.what: The action-RPG arena demo with GPU lighting, in four views.

entries.title: Starter games
entries.what: The file to hand an AI model: the engine, its API card and five small games. The kits are one game each.

entries.title: Scarfrunner
entries.what: The side-scrolling prototype that came before the engine.

sections.title: Temporary
sections.empty: Nothing here right now. One-off comparisons and experiments land here, with the date and the question each one answers, and are deleted once it is settled.

entries.title: Shapes vs props
entries.question: Are 3D models converted to shapes worth building, next to our flat props?
entries.what: Twelve free 3D models (Kenney and KayKit, CC0) converted to shapes and drawn by the engine in every view and turning, beside the hero and our closest flat prop, ranked from the best case to the worst, with what is off and what would fix it.

entries.title: Free camera room
entries.question: What does a free camera look like in our engine, and which objects hold up when you turn it?
entries.what: A small room with four pillars, crates and the hero walking a lap. Drag to turn and tilt, zoom, move up and down, then fix the camera anywhere and copy its code or link. The crates switch between a converted 3D shape, today's flat prop and the engine's plain box. Fly mode (G) is a first-person camera on a small renderer of its own, to show what the engine can't do and what carries over.

entries.title: 3D world lab
entries.question: Can our characters, animation and look live in a real 3D world (three.js r182 and Rapier), with all its art drawn by code, and stay easy for AI agents to work on?
entries.what: A stone room in real 3D (three.js r182 on WebGPU, or WebGL 2 by itself, and Rapier physics), every texture and shape drawn by code. The hero walks a lap or you play it (move, swing, dash, knock the crates about); a mocap figure and Emberdeep's Dan stand by. Each character is a Card (the engine's own drawing on a card facing the camera) or a Puppet (3D parts on the same joints), or both side by side, in the engine's five fixed views or a free orbit, fly or chase camera. The plan and the trade-offs are in docs/LAB-3D.md.

entries.title: Stress test in 3D
entries.question: Head to head: how does the stress test hold up drawn by three.js in real 3D, next to our own 2D renderer?
entries.what: The stress test itself (the same game code: hall, hero, walkers, slimes, wisps, combat, waves, panel, metrics and benchmark) drawn by three.js r182 on WebGPU or WebGL 2 in place of the engine's canvas. The monsters are Cards (the engine's own drawing standing in the 3D hall) or Puppets (3D parts on the same joints, with torchlight and shadows). The engine's own camera (every view, side scrolling, custom, fixed), or a chase, first-person or fly camera, fixed anywhere. Filters: Comic cel or Pixel on the whole scene, the characters and objects, or the hall, with bloom and FXAA. Run the benchmark on both pages to compare.

entries.title: Stress test: 3D world
entries.question: What does the stress test become built from the ground up as a 3D game (three.js r182, Rapier physics, a hall written as text), sharing only the engine's animation system, and how does it hold up?
entries.what: The stress test's job done as a 3D game, its own way: every monster is a Rapier body (the crowd pushes and piles up by itself, big hits throw bodies into the air, crates and barrels fly), the hero walks, dashes and jumps onto low walls and galleries, monsters find their way up the stairs after him. The hall is the 2D one's layout written as ASCII text, with a raised rune dais and two galleries. Characters are Cards (the engine draws them) or Puppets, in the engine's views (perspective or orthographic), side scrolling with depth, chase, first person, fly or fixed; filters as on the 3D stress test. The benchmark adds a physics column.
